def token_dag_game(n, edges, tokens):
    """Two players play a token game on a directed acyclic graph.

    The graph has n nodes labeled 1..n and a list of directed edges,
    each given as a pair [u, v] meaning an edge from u to v. The graph
    is guaranteed acyclic, with no self-loops and no duplicate edges.
    tokens[i] is the starting node of token i; several tokens may
    occupy the same node (tokens never block each other).

    Players First and Second alternate turns, First moving first. On a
    turn, a player picks any single token and moves it along one
    outgoing edge of that token's current node. A player who cannot
    move any token loses.

    Both players play optimally. If Second wins, return the string
    'Second'. Otherwise return one winning first move as a tuple
    (i, v), meaning: move token i (0-based index into tokens) to node
    v. If several first moves win, return the lexicographically
    smallest pair (i, v).

    Bounds: 1 <= n <= 200, 0 <= len(edges) <= n*(n-1)//2,
    1 <= len(tokens) <= 200. The combined game state space is far too
    large for direct game search.

    >>> token_dag_game(2, [[1, 2]], [1])
    (0, 2)
    >>> token_dag_game(4, [[1, 2], [1, 3], [2, 4], [3, 4]], [1])
    'Second'
    >>> token_dag_game(3, [[1, 2], [2, 3]], [2, 1])
    (0, 3)
    """
